prompts: The owner's gaming rig hitches every few seconds even though the average frame rate looks fine, and the 1% lows are poor. A one-minute frame capture, a sensor log, a dump of the rig's settings and the owner's notes are in {WS}. That rig is not this machine: everything about it is in these files, and nothing is to be applied to this host. Find what causes the hitches and which setting changes fix them within the owner's constraints. Record in {WS}/result.json: avg_fps, low_1pct_fps, cause and changes (a list of {setting, from, to}).
answers:
[goal] Find the hitch cause in rig arena-01 from the capture + sensor log + settings, propose constraint-respecting fixes, write ./result.json.

[action] Parsed capture/presentmon.csv (8238 frames, 60.0 s) and capture/sensors.csv (61 samples, same clock). Grouped slow frames into bursts, aligned burst times to sensor seconds, checked render/present-API times, dropped frames, SyncInterval, GPU clocks/link, and the Defender/disk spikes. Wrote result.json (validated as JSON). No browser or apps opened, nothing to close; nothing applied to this host.

[result]
- Measured: avg_fps 137.3 (mean 7.284 ms), 1% low 45.4 FPS (p99 22.05 ms), per the owner's method.
- Cause: PCIe ASPM L1 on the GPU root port (`pcie_aspm_rp1_gpu=L1`). 15 stall bursts of exactly 12 frames at 21-23 ms, starting 2.40, 6.40, 10.40 ... 58.40 s (period 4.0 s), matching 1:1 the 15 sensor samples with `gpu_pcie_link_state=L1` (seconds 2, 6, ... 58); all other seconds are L0. During stalls `MsUntilRenderComplete` stays ~5 ms and `MsInPresentAPI` ~0.3 ms, so CPU/GPU work did not grow, the extra ~15 ms/frame is link exit latency. Only 2.2% of frames are hit, so the mean looks fine while p99 collapses.
- Ruled out with data: Defender burst (s 43-45, MsMpEng, disk 80-94%, DPC 396-455 us) and disk spikes (s 13, 27, 52) produced no frame above 7.8 ms; no dropped frames; vsync off (SyncInterval=0) so not vblank waits; link stayed Gen5 x4 and clocks ~2.7 GHz, so the fixed x4 width is not the trigger.
- Fix: one change, `pcie_aspm_rp1_gpu: L1 -> disabled` (BIOS link power management, not an overclock). Gen5 x4 and XMP/PBO/core ratio untouched, so both constraints hold.
- Expected: excluding the stall bursts the capture's own frames give mean 6.955 ms / p99 7.66 ms, i.e. ~143.8 avg and ~130.6 FPS 1% low. That is arithmetic on the existing capture, not a re-measurement.
- Assumptions stated in result.json: shared clock means sensor second N covers t=N.0-N.999; the 4.0 s period is the platform ASPM timer; rp0 NVMe ASPM, Balanced plan and Defender left alone because they show no timing correlation.

[how I know] The evidence is the exact 15-for-15 alignment between stall bursts and L1 samples, the unchanged render time inside the stalls, and the absence of any frame spike at the times of the competing suspects (Defender, disk).

[next] Owner applies the ASPM change in BIOS and re-runs the same 1-minute PresentMon replay to confirm 1% lows near 130 FPS; if L1 is required elsewhere on that root port, the fallback is a platform ASPM-off/performance link-power option on rp1 only.
